models_evaluated: plastic surgery website AI chatbots (commercial platforms, unspecified)

links.outcome: Chatbot recognition and triage of emergent plastic surgery scenarios
links.effect: Emergent sensitivity 20%, NPV 0.71, false negative rate 80.0%; emergent cases mostly mislabeled as urgent; kappa 0.47 with physician classification.
links.quote: Emergent classifications were most mislabeled as urgent, with a low sensitivity (20%), negative predictive value (0.71), and high false negative rate (80.0%).

links.outcome: Recognition of emergent situations and appropriate escalation by chatbots
links.effect: Emergent sensitivity 20%, false negative rate 80.0%; over half of conversations required human-provider escalation.
links.quote: Emergent classifications were most mislabeled as urgent, with a low sensitivity (20%), negative predictive value (0.71), and high false negative rate (80.0%).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of real-world deployed chatbots on plastic surgery websites using standardized simulated patient scenarios to assess clinical triage accuracy and escalation trends.
